subject.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying

question: Should OpenClaw keep `llm_input` and `llm_output` observational and introduce capability-specific interception hooks, or redefine the existing hooks despite runtime differences?
rationale: The existing hooks are shipped public API, and Codex cannot faithfully implement every proposed result field at this lifecycle point; choosing the permanent compatibility and capability model requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Add capability-specific interception
options.body: Preserve the shipped observational hooks and design separate modifying hooks whose supported fields are explicit for each runtime.

options.title: Redefine existing hooks
options.body: Accept the compatibility change only after narrowing unsupported fields, completing all runners, documenting capability differences, and proving upgrades live.

options.title: Pause interception support
options.body: Defer the feature until a concrete owner-sponsored plugin use case establishes the required cross-runtime contract.

recommendation.title: Add capability-specific interception
recommendation.body: Preserve the shipped observational hooks and design separate modifying hooks whose supported fields are explicit for each runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and concentrated history show the strongest current ownership signal across both plugin contracts and agent runtimes.
